A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GA-Rollback work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated or renamed material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, threshold and waiting-step analyses, and multi-trial results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, GPT-4o results, expanded ablations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The generator-assistant procedure, environment restoration, feedback-confidence filtering and waiting rule remain unchanged. Wait-Info renames wait-k. The newly documented rollback-attempt limit and fuller prompt templates do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Game of 24, ALFWorld and Webshop with the same task requirements and environments. The additional analyses and GPT-4o evaluation reuse this coverage; GPT-4o adds a model setting.

E2.justification: v3 adds CoT throughout the three-model, three-task comparison in Table 1 and introduces a dedicated ToT-BFS comparison on Game of 24 in Table 2. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives to include standalone chain-of-thought prompting and tree search.

E3.justification: v3 adds GPT-4o evaluation on 200 Webshop instances, cross-task average success rate, token/runtime metrics and a rollback-attempt sweep from 1 to 8. The original 500-instance evaluations, ALFWorld test split, generation limits and temperature remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Feedback-threshold analysis expands from Webshop to ALFWorld, and component-removal and assistant-size ablations expand to Game of 24. Appendix B.3 adds computational-cost analysis and rollback-budget sensitivity. The existing multi-trial success-rate analysis, waiting-step curves and case studies are retained, including material moved into the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Reflexion trials are successive task-solving attempts, and feedback-confidence density estimation already appears in v1; extending those plots does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds CoT, ToT-BFS and GPT-4o results, expanded ablation and threshold results, and token/runtime and rollback-budget measurements. Table 1 changes Qwen GA-Rollback's ALFWorld success rate from 88.1% to 89.6%, although Table 3 and Figure 4 retain 88.1%; the new reported average of 48.8% also conflicts with that row's values. Additional Webshop reward-by-trial entries from v1's supplementary table disappear, while the success-rate curves remain.

T1.justification: The trajectory and rollback definitions, feedback-confidence equation and Webshop reward formula are retained. Added waiting-horizon notation and information-bandwidth discussion introduce no substantive mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The waiting contribution's novelty framing shifts: v1's conclusion describes adapting wait-k, whereas v3 describes introducing Wait-Info and removes its stated inspiration in Section 3.3. The central claims about rollback, benchmark performance and plug-and-play compatibility otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of advantages over tree search and interprets the new cost analysis as supporting a six-attempt trade-off. It also recasts waiting as information-bandwidth scheduling and predicts broader applicability. The existing explanations of trajectory difficulties and the stated limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies NVIDIA HGX H20 96G GPUs and a maximum of six rollback attempts per task. Appendix D explicitly adds the current-trajectory placeholder to all assistant templates. These improve implementation disclosure; the code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Ma et al. wait-k attribution, replaces Voyager and Auto-GPT references with two translation-related works, and adds a direct contrast with the already cited Tree of Thoughts approach. The broader positioning around LLM agents and self-correction remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 consistently renames wait-k to Wait-Info, rewrites the waiting-strategy discussion, moves multi-trial analysis from Section 4.3 to Appendix B.2 and reorganizes the results and case-study appendices. The abstract and most introductory and methodological prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The presentation changes substantially: Table 1 gains CoT rows and an average column, the ablation table gains a task column, and the feedback figure expands from two to four panels. v3 adds comparison and cost tables and a rollback-budget figure, relocates the multi-trial plot, and removes v1's two detailed supplementary tables.

improvement.justification: The added comparator evaluations and expanded ablations strengthen empirical support, while Tables 2 and 5 and Figure 7 quantify computational overhead left unmeasured in v1. These gains are moderated by lost detailed multi-trial rewards, less explicit waiting-strategy attribution and inconsistent Qwen ALFWorld reporting, including the unreconciled 48.8% average. Overall, v3 provides a modestly stronger basis for assessing the method and its practical costs.
